# Accordion

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

navigation and disclosure · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a list of questions or sections, where a reader opens the one they need. Every answer is
in the HTML from the start, so a crawler reads it and the browser's search finds it.

```ts
import { AccordionItem, AccordionRoot } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<AccordionRoot defaultValue={['install']}>
  <AccordionItem value="install" title="How do I install a component?" headingLevel={2}>
    <p>Run npx topclassui add accordion.</p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="arabic" title="Does it work in Arabic?" headingLevel={2}>
    <p>Yes. The caret moves to the left edge.</p>
  </AccordionItem>
</AccordionRoot>
```

- **Parts.** Two flat names and no bare `Accordion`: `AccordionRoot` and `AccordionItem`.
  Each passes the rest of its props to the element it draws: the box, and the item.
- **An item.** `value` names it and `title` is the text of its trigger: both are required.
  Its children are the panel.
- **Open at first.** `defaultValue={['install']}` on the root: the `value` of each item
  that starts open.
- **One at a time.** The default. Opening an item closes the open one. Pressing the open
  one closes it too, so every item can be closed.
- **`multiple`.** Opening an item leaves the others as they are.
- **The heading level.** `headingLevel` on each item, 2 to 6, default 3. Pick one more than
  the heading above the accordion: 2 under the page's `<h1>`, 3 under an `<h2>`.
- **The title.** Text, or inline elements such as an icon or a `Badge`. No link and no
  button: the title sits inside a `<button>`, where HTML allows neither. Put the link in
  the panel. An empty title leaves the button with no name.
- **A long title** wraps onto more lines. It is never cut.
- **Wide content.** A table wider than the box scrolls sideways inside its panel. Once the
  page has hydrated, the panel is a tab stop for as long as it scrolls.
- **Find in page.** A closed panel is `hidden="until-found"`: the browser's search, a link
  to an `#id` inside it and a text fragment all open it, and the trigger follows. This
  starts once the page has hydrated; before that a closed panel is plain `hidden`.
- **`hiddenUntilFound={false}`** on the root takes closed panels out of the page.
  `keepMounted` then keeps them, hidden from the search as well.
- **Disabled.** `disabled` on an item, or on the root for all of them. The trigger keeps
  its place in the tab order and says that it is disabled.
- **Keyboard.** Tab moves from trigger to trigger. Enter and Space toggle. There are no
  arrow keys: Base UI 1.8.0 dropped them, as the ARIA Authoring Practices did.
- **A screen reader** hears the trigger as a button in a heading, expanded or collapsed,
  an open panel as a region named by its title, and a closed panel not at all.
- **Motion.** A panel fades in and out in 150 ms. Its height does not animate: what is
  below it moves in one step. Reduced motion removes the fade.
- **An accordion in a panel** works. Give its items the next `headingLevel`.
- **From a server page.** Write the title and the children there. Pass text, booleans and
  `defaultValue`. Pass no function: `value` with `onValueChange`, and `onOpenChange`, need
  a `'use client'` file.

### What Base UI gives

| Prop | On | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | `AccordionRoot` | The open items, as an array of their `value`s: yours or its own. |
| `multiple` | `AccordionRoot` | More than one item open at a time. Default `false`. |
| `disabled` | `AccordionRoot`, `AccordionItem` | Ignores a press. |
| `hiddenUntilFound`, `keepMounted` | `AccordionRoot` | Whether a closed panel stays in the page. |
| `onOpenChange` | `AccordionItem` | Called when this item opens or closes. |

### Not built

A height animation, `type` and `collapsible` (use `multiple`; an open item can always be
closed), `variant`, a data-driven `Accordion`, one `headingLevel` for a whole root,
`loopFocus` and `orientation` (deprecated in Base UI 1.8.0, where they move no focus).

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  AccordionRoot,
  AccordionItem,
} from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `title` on `AccordionItem`, `value` on `AccordionItem`. Every other prop below is optional.

### AccordionRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hiddenUntilFound` | no | `boolean` | `true` | AccordionRoot: closed panels stay in the HTML, where find-in-page and a crawler read them. |

### AccordionItem

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | **yes** | `ReactNode` | - | The text of the trigger. It sits inside a button: text and inline elements, never a link or a control. |
| `value` | **yes** | `string` | - | The name of this item in the root's value and defaultValue. |
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | What the panel holds. It stays in the HTML while the panel is closed. |
| `headingLevel` | no | `integer`, min 2, max 6 | `3` | AccordionItem: the level of the heading its trigger sits in, clamped to h2 through h6. |

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
